subject: The shipped Git attention surface exposes shared work and gives agents authorized evidence for a targeted plan.
reader: Parker owns Terminal Delight, approved the Git coordination design, and wants what shipped and what the tests prove; he does not read Rust.

sections.heading: Git coordination
sections.text:
Several agents can share a checkout or change the same file on different branches. Terminal Delight now shows where that work is connected, why it needs attention, and what an agent should inspect next. 

 Verified locally Application + agent read tools 2026-10-18

sections.heading: 01 Notice work that needs attention
sections.text:
01 · A clear selection keeps attention elsewhere visible 

 ▦ GIT · ▲ WARNING · 1 project · PARTIAL 

 SELECTED Client Portal ✓ Clear 
 ELSEWHERE IN THIS WINDOW Terminal Delight ▲ Three checkouts touch relay.rs Packaging checkout unavailable 

 Selection cannot silence another project's warning. This drawing uses the native fixture's observations. The permanent rail carries urgency and coverage; checkout counts and idle inventory live inside inspection. Native capture ↗ measured 

The old rotating ticker is gone. One GIT signal summarizes the projects in this window—even when the selected project is clear. In this example, Client Portal is clear while Terminal Delight has overlapping work. Click GIT to find the cause. Urgent projects come first, unread projects precede clear ones, and a project can expand into ranked group previews before you open it. 

 02 · Preview the connections before drilling in 

 ▾ Terminal Delight ▲ WARNING partial 

 ↳ relay.rs 3 checkouts · shared file + shared checkout ▲ Warning 

 ↳ palette.rs 2 checkouts · shared file ◇ Caution 

Packaging unread checkout unavailable · membership incomplete 

 Client Portal ✓ CLEAR 

 The two observed groups are different connections. Missing evidence can join them later; a falling group count does not establish reduced friction. The native project view keeps that uncertainty visible. measured

sections.heading: 02 Follow the connection to its cause
sections.text:
The first group connects three checkouts through a file named relay.rs. Open it to see the relationship: the panes, their checkout roots and branches, and each file's change sources appear together. Exact Git references and checkout metrics unfold in place. The same inspector can then take you to a participant’s pane. 

 03 · Four panes, three checkouts, one shared-file hotspot 

 | 
 | Pane | Checkout / branch | relay.rs evidence 

 | Render A | render
 feature/render | committed unstaged 

 | Host B, C | host
 feature/host | unstaged 
 Two panes share this checkout. 

 | CLI D | cli
 feature/cli | staged 

 Known-member paths complete Project membership partial 

 Pane occupancy does not establish file authorship. The live fixture also supplies an untracked path in the shared host checkout. A separate fixture verifies two named panes sharing one known session in both native rows and MCP. Native evidence ↗ measured 

 04 · Pane navigation keeps the inspector's keyboard 

 Project → Relay group → Focus Host B → Esc Project → Esc Projects → Esc Closed 

 Repeated Escape returns through the inspector after focusing a pane. The real-window check exercises this without forcing focus back between keys. Each depth retains its scroll position, and arrow selection scrolls into view. 390-pixel capture ↗ measured

sections.heading: 03 Give an agent the evidence
sections.text:
Once the cause is visible, a person can direct an agent to investigate it. Ctrl+C copies the evidence that agent is permitted to see, together with an exact read request. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) exposes the same observations through four read tools. An agent can also start with coordination_overview , follow the returned group request, and propose a plan against the named roots and measured references. 
 05 · Background observations 

 Git collection stays in the existing background worker. Four change sources keep separate coverage, and an unavailable checkout remains an explicit observation gap. code inspected 06 · Authorized relationships 

 Authorization comes before groups, identifiers and history. Shared places form connected groups; two clones with one remote do not become one shared object database. code inspected 07 · A shared snapshot 

 In a fully exposed window, native inspection and MCP use the same authorized snapshot. Scope changes start fresh agent history; operator history is kept separate. code inspected 

 Restricted exposure keeps file evidence unavailable. Git cannot attribute a filesystem change to the pane permitted to disclose it. Agents still see permitted occupancy. Once a window has held an off-limits pane, the conservative file restriction lasts for that window's lifetime. Human inspection can show more; copying for an agent stays inside the authorized projection. 

The four read tools share the existing running-window MCP relay. They expose observed causes, project details, joined group evidence and changes since a scoped version. A checkout-specific project read also pages file and conflict evidence for an isolated alert. Those permissions and missing observations are part of the behavior the tests must prove. 
 Read contract and captured response ↗

sections.heading: 04 Prove the warning can be trusted
sections.text:
08 · The tests reject false confidence 

 Authorization filter deliberately removed Assertion failed as expected 

 Incomplete coverage deliberately called complete Assertion failed as expected 

 Restored source · default terminal core 2,445 passed · 9 ignored 

 Restored source · fallback terminal core 2,398 passed · 9 ignored 

 Both injected faults fail assertions, then the restored source passes. The coordination checks cover raw filenames and renames, four change sources, shared sessions, physical clone identity, cross-project worktrees, coverage bridges, scope-local history, bounded cursors, and Git subprocess failures. measured 

The sparse fixture has 100 checkouts and 10,000 paths. The dense fixture retains 11 hotspots across 40 checkouts. Real-window checks cover project and group navigation, pane focus, copied agent context, permission cycling and narrow layouts. 

A loaded run reproduced the existing host-test race: it read the child's environment before exec. The fixture now waits for the executable transition, then checks the same identity fields. Twenty full unit-suite stress runs passed. With those checks complete, the remaining step is to use the evidence to assign work. 
 Method, limits and full results ↗

sections.heading: 05 Investigate, then direct the work
sections.text:
The native implementation is built. Release verification is in progress. 

Open GIT, choose a project or group, then copy context or focus an existing pane. Agents use the read tools to investigate and plan; the authorized agent performs the Git work. 

Release binary built and verified locally. Installation follows the single pull request and required CI checks. 

The approved entry point, signal policy and first-release direction remain the basis of this implementation. Optional line analysis and push notifications are outside this release.
